overview: People who work as officers on U.S. commercial ships must pass a Coast Guard exam to earn a merchant mariner credential, a license to serve in those jobs. This bill would update the working group that reviews that exam, adding at least two people who passed it within the past five years and a representative of the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy, and requiring it to meet at least once a year. The working group would have to approve new exam questions before they are used, and would review the exam for outdated or redundant topics, current industry practices, and overlap with international training standards. The Coast Guard would then have to write a plan to modernize the exam, including updating testing methods and tracking pass and fail rates, and brief Congress within a year. As of October 29, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say the mariner exam has fallen behind modern ship technology and testing practices, and that giving recent test-takers and educators a voice will make it fairer and more relevant.
against: Critics say requiring a working group to sign off on every new question could slow updates to the exam, and that changes meant to modernize it should not lower the bar for safety at sea.
